name: Dripify
summary: Cloud-based LinkedIn outreach automation: drip sequences of connection requests, messages, InMails and profile views, with configurable daily limits and a built-in email finder.
best_for: sales teams that already run LinkedIn outreach, understand that automation breaches LinkedIn's terms, and accept that risk with their eyes open: the cloud architecture means sequences run with your browser closed and no extension injected into your session
skip_if: your LinkedIn account is not expendable, since a restriction can be permanent and no tool can promise otherwise; or you are tempted by the 75-a-day ceiling, because the vendor's own advice is roughly a fifth of that
honest_knock: Understand what you are buying before the price matters: LinkedIn prohibits this entire product category. Its User Agreement bans using 'bots or other unauthorized automated methods' to 'send or redirect messages', and its prohibited-software page says members using such tools 'risk having their accounts restricted or shut down'. There is no carve-out for cloud tools or low volumes, and Dripify is not an outlier here: every competitor sits on the same side of that line. Dripify's own documentation is candid about the consequence, warning that LinkedIn 'may issue warnings, temporary restrictions, or even permanent bans', and it publishes a recovery procedure for exactly that scenario. Two things follow. First, the advertised ceiling is not a working speed: the app allows up to 75 connection requests a day, while Dripify's own setup guide tells beginners to run 10 to 15, and brand-new accounts 2 to 5, building up 10 to 20 percent a week. Anyone buying on the headline number is buying capacity they are told not to use. Second, Activity Control sits on the $79 Advanced tier. It is the feature Dripify names as its best protection, and it adjusts your pace automatically. The pricing page read on 13 November 2026 lists built-in LinkedIn protection on Pro and advanced LinkedIn protection on Advanced; we have not re-checked whether Activity Control itself still sits only on Advanced, so ask before you rely on automatic pacing on Pro. And when a vendor writes that a feature 'makes sure your LinkedIn account won't get flagged', read that as a claim about a third party's enforcement decisions that no vendor can actually guarantee.

pricing.plans_source: hand-curated from the vendor's pricing page
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-08-26 on their own pricing page — note that dripify.io now redirects to dripify.com) Three tiers, priced per user: Pro $59 and Advanced $79 per user per month billed annually, plus an Enterprise tier that is quote-only. The $39 Basic tier we recorded in August is gone from the page as of the 13 November 2026 reading. Month to month the two paid tiers read $79 and $99 per user; both columns sit in the page and the FAQ repeats all four numbers in words. A 7-day free trial runs without a credit card. So the 'up to 35% off' the toggle advertises is real but front-loaded: you pay a year up front to get it, and the discount shrinks as you go up the range — about 25 percent on Pro and 20 on Advanced. What each tier buys is unusually consequential here. On the 10 October reading the page printed the daily quotas (75 connection requests, 100+ messages, 30 Sales Navigator InMails and 200+ profile views a day on Pro and Advanced); the 13 November pricing page no longer prints them. Unlimited drip campaigns start at Pro, which adds a dedicated inbox, CSV export and the webhook and HubSpot integrations, and Advanced adds multi-team management, advanced LinkedIn protection, lead tagging, step analytics and evergreen leads. Every tier includes 100 email-finder credits a month and the top-ups are priced openly: 1,000 credits $29, 2,000 $49, 5,000 $69, 10,000 $99. One seat connects one LinkedIn account, so five reps means five seats, and ten or more seats goes through sales. Re-read 10 October 2026: prices and daily quotas unchanged, and Pro now also lists an Open API and an MCP server. Re-read 13 November 2026: Basic is gone; Pro now lists built-in LinkedIn protection, 24/7 live support, an open API and an MCP server, and Advanced adds team management, advanced LinkedIn protection, lead tagging, step analytics, A/B testing and evergreen leads. A partner mail of 9 November 2026 said Dripify is now available on Pro and Advanced plans only, which matches the page.

compare_with.name: Expandi
compare_with.why: the closest head-to-head: both are cloud-based with a regional dedicated IP, so the 'cloud versus extension' framing you will read in affiliate roundups does not actually separate them. The real difference is the pricing model: Expandi sells one Business plan with everything included at $99 per user a month, 20 percent off annually, while Dripify tiers both quotas and safety features. Watch the gap that roundups quote: Dripify's annual rate ($59 on Pro) set against Expandi's monthly one ($99). Month against month it is $79 to $99 versus $99, and at the top of Dripify's range the two cost the same. Expandi's price list was read on 2026-07-24 and Dripify's on 2026-11-13; verify them yourself before you buy.
